newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-TRIUMPHANT DAVIS CUP WINNERS FETED BY PARISIANS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TRIUMPHANT DAVIS CUP WINNERS FETED BY PARISIANS.

text.p: Thousands of Parisians lined the Champs Elysees on Tuesday to fete the triumphant French Davis Cup team.

President Jacques Chirac, who hosted a reception for the players at the Elysee palace, said of the quartet who beat Sweden 3-2 in a marathon final at the weekend "They made us experience astonishing moments. We are infinitely proud of them."
The players -- Guy Forget, Arnaud Boetsch, Cedric Pioline and Guillaume Raoux -- and captain Yannick Noah were driven down the Champs Elysees in two open-top cars to cheers from the crowds.

They then drove to the Roland Garros stadium, home of the French Open, to place the Davis Cup at the foot of a statue of the late Rene Lacoste, who helped France to win the trophy six successive times between 1927 and 1932. Lacoste died in October.
Rain, which had been pouring down on Paris since the weekend, stopped just in time for the parade and fans brought the players' cars to a standstill as they clamoured for autographs.

"It's incredible, when we were told we were going down (the Champs Elysees) I didn't think there would be a crowd," said Boetsch, whose epic victory over Nicklas Kulti in the fifth match of the final in Malmo gave France the cup for the eighth time.

It was only the third time in 20 years that a winning team had been feted on the Champs Elysees. The honour was accorded to 1976 European Cup soccer finalists Saint-Etienne and last season's Cup Winners' Cup champions Paris Saint-Germain.
